sourcedFrom: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ (NOT READ)
cleanIntro: Taylor's prints its own owner's manual for the TC73 9mm, and every step below is quoted from it. The TC73 is a modern 1873-pattern lever action with a tubular magazine, side plates, a dust cover and a lever lock. The book publishes one disassembly procedure, done in order: stock off, side plates off, then the lever group, the triggerguard assembly and the breech block. You need gunsmith screwdriver bits, a plastic-headed gunsmith's hammer and a punch set. Taylor's own limits are plain: the link sets, the triggerguard assembly and the extractors stay together, and nothing comes apart past the steps here.

steps.title: This book covers the 9mm TC73 only
steps.action: This book covers the TC73 in 9mm and no other caliber. The caliber is marked on the barrel; check it reads 9MM before you follow these steps.
steps.quote: This owner’s manual is for the Model TC73 rifle in 9MM caliber only.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Introduction, p.2

steps.title: Lever the action repeatedly to eject every round
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and your finger away from the trigger. Work the lever again and again until no more rounds come out. The rounds in the tube feed up one at a time, so keep levering until the rifle stops ejecting anything.
steps.quote: While keeping the muzzle pointed in a safe direction, and your finger away from the trigger, repeatedly lever the action to eject all the unfired rounds from the gun.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Unloading the Gun, p.18
steps.warn: WHEN UNLOADING YOUR RIFLE, ALWAYS KEEP THE MUZZLE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION AND YOUR FINGERS AWAY FROM THE TRIGGER.

steps.title: Lever open, chamber and lower tube area checked
steps.action: With the lever open, look into the chamber and down at the lower magazine tube area. The follower butt shows there when the tube is empty. If you see a round anywhere, you are not done.
steps.quote: When no more rounds are being ejected, you can check to be sure the firearm is completely unloaded by levering the action open and inspecting the chamber and lower magazine tube area for any remaining rounds of ammunition.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Unloading the Gun, p.18

steps.title: Hammer to half-cock
steps.action: Close the action and bring the hammer to half-cock: it is drawn back slightly and clicks into place, no longer resting on the firing pin extension. Levering the action leaves the hammer at full-cock, so check where it is before you go on.
steps.quote: Once unloaded, the gun should be stored with the hammer in the half-cock position.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Firing the Gun, p.18

steps.title: Rifle unloaded, action closed
steps.action: Confirm again that the rifle is unloaded and pointed somewhere safe, and leave the action closed to start. Work on a clean surface. Taylor's says to follow its steps in order, or you could damage the gun.
steps.aside: Tools required for proper disassembly are quality gunsmith screwdriver bits (or hollow ground type bits), a gunsmithing hammer with a plastic head, and a punch set.
steps.quote: Make sure your gun is unloaded and pointed in a safe direction. Leave the action closed.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Lever lock turned fully out of the way
steps.action: Turn the lever lock 180 degrees so it is clear of the lever. You will need to work the lever later. Turning the lock once the gun is apart lets the lever lock spring come off the triggerguard.
steps.quote: Make sure your lever lock is turned 180 degrees completely out of the way of the lever so that you can lever the action later on, turning this later while the gun is disassembled will make the lever lock spring come off the triggerguard.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Both buttstock screws out
steps.action: Take out the bottom buttstock screw, then the top tang screw. Use bits that fit the slots properly; a poor fit marks the screws and the finish.
steps.quote: Remove the bottom buttstock screw. - Remove the top tang buttstock screw.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Buttstock wiggled off the tang
steps.action: Work the buttstock off the receiver with a gentle wiggle, not a pry. It fits the receiver very tightly, and forcing it cracks the wood around the tang.
steps.quote: Once you remove those screws you will need to “wiggle” or pull off the buttstock. Extreme care must be taken while doing this or you will damage the buttstock by cracking the wood area around the tang.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26
steps.warn: Extreme care must be taken while doing this or you will damage the buttstock by cracking the wood area around the tang.

steps.title: Rifle laid flat, non-loading-gate side up
steps.action: Lay the rifle on a flat surface with the side plate that has no loading gate facing you. Taylor's suggests a folded clean rag under the receiver to raise it a little, which makes the side plates and small pins easier to handle.
steps.quote: Once the buttstock is off, make sure you have the gun laying on a flat surface with the non-loading gate side plate facing up to you.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Side plate screw loosened, first plate popped off
steps.action: Unscrew the side plate screw all the way but leave it in its hole. Push lightly on the loose screw while you lift the rifle, and the opposite side plate pops off.
steps.quote: Unscrew the side plate screw completely but leave it in the hole. You will push on the loose screw slightly while lifting up on the rifle to pop the opposite side plate off.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Rifle flipped, second side plate tapped off
steps.action: Turn the rifle over and tap the remaining side plate off from the inside, through the opposite side. Working from the inside keeps you off the outer finish. The loading gate can stay on its plate unless you need to clean that area; one screw holds it.
steps.quote: Flip the gun over and you can pop off the other side plate by tapping the inside of it from the opposite side. This allows you to easily remove the side plates without damaging the external finish.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Both link sets out, kept whole
steps.action: Pull or tap the link sets out of both sides of the receiver. Each one comes out as a unit and stays that way.
steps.quote: Pull out or tap out the link sets from both sides. Do not disassemble the link sets.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26
steps.warn: Do not disassemble the link sets.

steps.title: Lever pin out
steps.action: Remove the pin at the top of the lever.
steps.quote: Remove the lever pin in the top of the lever.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Lever and lifter spring screws out
steps.action: Take out the lever spring screw and the lifter spring screw. Be ready for the two springs: they drop out as soon as the screws are free. Note how each spring leg sits so it can go back the same way.
steps.quote: Remove the lever and lifter spring screws. When you remove these the lever and lifter springs will fall out.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Lever screw out, lever pulled
steps.action: Remove the lever screw, then pull the lever out of the receiver.
steps.quote: Remove the lever screw. - Pull the lever out.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Lifter arm and carrier block out
steps.action: Pull the lifter arm out, then the carrier block.
steps.quote: Pull the lifter arm out. - Pull the carrier block out.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Hammer to half-cock
steps.action: Put the hammer at half-cock before the triggerguard comes out.
steps.quote: Put the hammer in the half-cock position.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Triggerguard assembly out, kept whole
steps.action: Remove both triggerguard screws and ease the triggerguard assembly out of the receiver. It is cleaned and serviced as one piece.
steps.quote: Remove both of the triggerguard screws. - Carefully pull the triggerguard assembly out of the receiver. Do not disassemble the triggerguard assembly.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26
steps.warn: Do not disassemble the triggerguard assembly. You should be able to clean/service the assembly as-is without taking it apart.

steps.title: Dust cover back, screw out, guide block free
steps.action: Slide the dust cover all the way back to open it and remove the dust cover screw. The guide block under the cover is now free to come out.
steps.quote: Slide the dust cover all the way back and open. Remove the dust cover screw. This will allow the dust cover guide block to come out.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.26

steps.title: Dust cover eased back until the sphere shows, then left
steps.action: Slide the dust cover a little further back, carefully, until the small sphere pops up into the screw hole, and stop there. The cover stays put on the sphere's tension and does not need to come off for cleaning.
steps.quote: We do not recommend removing the dust cover further from this point as it has a small spring & sphere under it which can get lost and can be difficult to re-install.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Rear breech block pin out
steps.action: Remove the rear breech block pin.
steps.quote: Remove the rear breech block pin.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Firing pin extension pressed, stop wedge pulled
steps.action: Hold the breech block and press the firing pin extension in at the same time. With it depressed, the firing pin extension stop wedge slides out of the bottom of the breech block.
steps.quote: Hold on to the breech block and depress the firing pin extension at the same time. When the firing pin extension is depressed, this will allow you to pull the firing pin extension stop wedge out of the bottom of the breech block.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Firing pin extension out
steps.action: Pull out the firing pin extension. Note which way it faces; it goes back the same way round.
steps.quote: Pull out the firing pin extension.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Receiver inverted, breech block drawn out
steps.action: Turn the receiver upside down so the dust cover is on the work surface, which makes the breech block easier to steer. Then draw the breech block back and out of the receiver.
steps.quote: Flip the receiver upside down so that the dust cover is facing down on the work surface. This makes it easier to maneuver the breech block in the receiver. - Carefully pull the breech block back and out of the receiver.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Firing pin and spring out of the breech block
steps.action: The firing pin and its spring come straight out of the breech block once it is free. Leave the extractors in the block.
steps.quote: When you pull out the breech block, the firing pin and firing pin spring will come right out of it. We do not recommend removing the extractors from the breech block as it is not needed for regular servicing/cleaning.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Magazine tube cap unscrewed slowly
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine tube cap slowly and keep a hold of it. The magazine spring pushes against it the whole way off.
steps.quote: Slowly remove the magazine tube cap, the spring will be tensioned under it while you are unscrewing it.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Magazine spring and follower out
steps.action: Pull the magazine spring and the follower out of the tube. The tube itself and the forend stay on the rifle.
steps.quote: Pull out the magazine spring and follower. - For regular servicing/cleaning you should not need to fully remove the magazine tube or forend past this point.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is the whole of Taylor's disassembly: buttstock, side plates, link sets, lever, both springs, lifter arm, carrier block, triggerguard assembly, dust cover guide block, breech block with firing pin extension, wedge, firing pin and spring, and the magazine spring and follower. The link sets, triggerguard assembly and extractors stay whole, and nothing comes apart further.
steps.quote: You have now disassembled your gun for any servicing or cleaning you need to do.
steps.cite: Model TC73 9MM Rifle Owner’s Manual — NOT READ — Disassembly Instructions, p.27
steps.warn: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL.

deepAbsentReason: The book publishes one disassembly procedure (pp.25–27), and the field strip above walks all of it. It ends on p.27 'You have now disassembled your gun for any servicing or cleaning you need to do.', followed by 'CAUTION: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR FIREARM APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL.' (p.27). It publishes no deeper procedure.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean the bore with a suitable cleaning rod and patch, taking care not to damage the muzzle crown
Light fouling comes out with a solvent-soaked patch; heavy fouling needs a bore brush and solvent first, then patches
⚠ Prolonged solvent immersion or use can damage the rifle
Wipe the bore dry with patches, then run lightly oiled patches through it against rust
Check the chamber for stuck cases or pieces of case

cleaning.name: MUZZLE THREADS & SIGHTS
tasks: Take off the muzzle thread protector and clean and lightly oil it and the barrel threads, or it can become hard to unthread
Check the front and rear sights are clean, lightly oiled and secure

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Clean the inside of the magazine tube and lightly oil it
A dirty magazine spring can be sprayed with solvent and blown dry with air
Clean the magazine tube cap threads

cleaning.name: ACTION PARTS & RECEIVER
tasks: Clean and lightly oil every action part, pin and screw; use a cleaning brush on heavily fouled parts
Clean the receiver inside and out, then lightly oil it
Inspect every part for wear or damage before assembly
Do not take apart the link sets, the triggerguard assembly or the extractors

cleaning.name: STOCKS & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the forend and buttstock with a dry rag
Do not get solvent or oil on the wooden stocks
After assembly, lightly oil the external metal surfaces before storage

reassembly: Every part clean and lightly oiled first. Refit the magazine follower, spring and tube cap; Taylor's suggests a small dab of non-permanent blue thread-locker on the cap.
Put the firing pin spring and a lightly oiled firing pin into the breech block. Lightly lubricate the tops of the arms and the end of the breech block where it touches the top inside of the receiver.
With the receiver upside down, slide the breech block all the way forward toward the chamber. Refit the firing pin extension the right way round and press it into the block again.
Refit the stop wedge up into the breech block, flat side against the block; seated properly it holds the firing pin extension. Refit the rear breech block pin so it sticks out evenly on both sides.

Slide the dust cover forward, pressing the sphere down if needed. Set the guide block under it, square side toward the hammer and flat side up — fitted wrong, the dust cover will not work and can cause an ammunition malfunction. Line up the holes and fit the dust cover screw.
Check the parts and screws in the triggerguard assembly are secure. With the hammer still at half-cock, refit the triggerguard assembly, holes lined up with the receiver, and fit its screws.

Put the hammer in the rested position. Refit the carrier block, then the lifter arm. Fit the lever slightly open so it lines up with the lifter arm, then fit the lever screw without over-tightening it, or the rifle becomes hard to lever.

Refit the lever and lifter springs with their screws, every spring leg seated properly before the screws go fully home. Refit the link set on the loading-gate side, and the loading gate if you removed it (a small dab of blue thread-locker on its screw).

Lightly lubricate the flat inside faces of the side plates, but not the loading gate itself. Hold the loading-gate side plate tight to the receiver while you turn the rifle over, refit the lever pin, then the other link set, wiggling the lever if needed to line things up.
Fit the last side plate and the side plate screw. Work the action to check everything functions before going further, and oil around the carrier block, levering to spread it.
If all is right, slide the buttstock back on with the same care as removal so the wood does not crack. Refit the top tang screw, then the bottom screw.
fncheck: With the rifle empty, work the action to make sure everything functions and feels correct. Close the dust cover and lever the action to check that the cover opens properly. If anything binds or feels wrong, stop and contact Taylor's rather than forcing it — never force a jammed action, which can bend the action parts.
